currentContext.strengths: Vertically integrated manufacturing from spinning to finished bed linen across four Indian facilities (Alte, Gokul Shirgaon, Bhilad, Kagal), enabling efficient capacity utilisation and operational synergies.|Diversified owned and licensed brand portfolio (Boutique Living, Layers, and the revived heritage brand Wamsutta, alongside licensed brands Fieldcrest, Waverly, Beautyrest and Tommy Hilfiger) supporting premiumisation and B2C/D2C channel diversification beyond traditional B2B.|Demonstrated customer-relationship durability: through the peak-tariff disruption of FY26 the Company retained every customer and fulfilled every order without cancellation, strengthening its standing from supplier to indispensable partner.|Local U.S. manufacturing footprint (Phoenix AZ, Kernersville NC, Columbus OH) brings production closer to its largest market (~70% of market exposure), improving fulfilment speed and supply-chain responsiveness, while U.S.-cotton content above 20% qualifies for proportionate tariff relief in the premium segment.|Broad sustainability/quality certification base (OEKO-TEX STeP, ISO 9001/14001/45001, LEED Green Building, NABL/ISO 17025) plus a leading ESG profile (S&P Global ESG score of 78, top 3 percentile globally in the sector) that supports trust with global retail customers.|Recognised export leadership — six consecutive TEXPROCIL Gold Trophies for the highest exports of bed sheets/bed linen in the cotton made-ups category.
currentContext.strategies: Indo Count 2.0 transformation: operations formally reclassified into a 'core business' (bed linen, sheets, fashion bedding, institutional bedding manufactured in Kolhapur and Bhilad) and 'new businesses' (utility bedding and the U.S. brand business), which scaled from 2% of revenue in FY23 to 19% in FY26.|Core business priorities for FY27: grow revenue toward ₹4,000 crore, recover margins as tariff-related discounts unwind, and accelerate geographic diversification into markets opened by the UK and EU Free Trade Agreements.|Medium-term ambition to double consolidated revenue toward a run rate of approximately ₹8,000 crore by 2028.|During the peak U.S. tariff disruption, the Company deliberately chose to protect customer relationships and market share over sales volume, sharing part of the tariff/Russian-oil-penalty impact with customers on a case-by-case basis.|Sustainability strategy under 'Business Plan 2030' (six pillars, mapped to UN SDGs and SBTi) is positioned as integral to long-term value creation, not a separate initiative.|This bundle contains no explicit dividend/reinvestment policy narrative; the only capital-allocation item present is a procedural Notice-of-AGM resolution to declare a Final Dividend of ₹1.50 (75%) per equity share of face value ₹2 for FY2025-26, continuing the Company's practice of an annual dividend.
currentContext.expansion: The largest capacity addition in FY26 was Indo Count's first and largest overseas greenfield manufacturing facility, at Kernersville, North Carolina, for utility bedding; it commenced commercial production in January 2026, adding 18 million pillows/year and taking combined U.S. pillow capacity to 31 million units alongside 1.5 million quilts, with the three U.S. facilities (Columbus OH, Phoenix AZ, Kernersville NC) together providing East Coast, Midwest and West Coast coverage. On the brand side, Wamsutta (the Company's fully owned legacy U.S. brand) was relaunched in July 2025 on a Direct-to-Consumer platform and reached all 50 U.S. states within 45 days; a new licensing agreement with Tommy Hilfiger for utility bedding was signed during the year, taking the licensed-brand count to six (Fieldcrest, Waverly, GAIAM, Jasper Conran, Beautyrest, Tommy Hilfiger). Domestically, the Boutique Living and Layers brands added 700 new counters in a single quarter, entered the bath and gifting segments, and now reach about 2,000 touchpoints, though the domestic business remains young at 2.25% of revenue with management expecting it to become a meaningful contributor over three to five years. Core business capacity utilisation stood at 60-65%, and the two existing U.S. utility bedding facilities were also running at 60-65% utilisation. Total capital expenditure during FY26 was ₹202 crore. Looking ahead, the Company has planned ₹250 crore of capital expenditure over the next 12-18 months, three-quarters funded by internal accruals, comprising ₹95 crore for a Zero Liquid Discharge facility at the Bhilad unit, ₹85 crore for a spinning brownfield expansion and modernisation, and ₹70 crore of maintenance capex, framed as support for the goal of doubling revenues by 2028.
currentContext.mdna: India-EU Free Trade Agreement, concluded January 2026, grants zero-duty access to the EU market for Indian textiles, apparel and made-ups, eliminating prior duties of 8-12% and restoring tariff parity with Bangladesh and Vietnam; expected to strengthen trade flows and improve long-term visibility for Indian home textile exporters.|Within U.S. cotton textiles, the home textiles segment (cotton bed linen, towels, made-ups) is projected to grow at an 8.9% CAGR, presenting a constructive medium-term demand backdrop for established Indian manufacturers serving the U.S. retail channel.|Bed linen remains Indo Count's dominant product category in the global home textiles market, with bathroom linen emerging as a faster-growing adjacency.|U.S. home textiles retail continues shifting toward omnichannel models, with rapid e-commerce and direct-to-consumer expansion enabling deeper customer reach and engagement.|India's structural advantages -- world's largest cotton producer, second-largest employer after agriculture, and an integrated cotton-to-finished-product value chain -- support established manufacturers amid the 'China-plus-one' sourcing realignment.|Government of India's Ministry of Textiles has outlined a roadmap to triple textile exports from ₹3 lakh crore today to ₹9 lakh crore by 2030, supported by stronger domestic manufacturing and broader global market outreach.|Growing global-buyer emphasis on eco-friendly and traceable cotton sourcing is emerging as a defining lever, presenting a premium opportunity for manufacturers with integrated procurement and certified traceability frameworks.|New businesses (utility bedding and the U.S. brand business) scaled from 2% of revenue in FY23 to 19% in FY26, reaching an annualised run rate above USD 100 million -- management frames this as a new revenue vertical approaching a fifth of total income built within three years.

risks.note: Tariffs on Indian textile exports to the U.S. swung from 10% to 25% to 50% and back to 10% within FY26, directly affecting the Company's cost competitiveness, pricing strategies, customer demand and supply-chain dynamics; as a significant exporter, the Company remains highly exposed to further shifts in global trade policy.

SWOT flags 'Export Market Concentration' as a threat -- the Company's strong presence in international markets exposes it to risks from changes in trade policies, tariff regimes, currency movements and global economic uncertainties.
SWOT weakness 'Dependence on Cotton' -- high reliance on cotton exposes the business to price volatility and climate-related supply fluctuations.

risks.risk: Ageing manufacturing technology and capital intensity
risks.note: SWOT weaknesses 'Outdated Technology' (continued reliance on ageing infrastructure may constrain productivity and the ability to meet evolving customer expectations) and 'Capital-Intensive Operations' (significant ongoing capex on technology and capacity expansion could pressure free cash flow).

SWOT weakness 'Compliance Gaps' (inconsistent adherence to global environmental and labour standards may affect export competitiveness) combined with the threat of 'Stricter Environmental Regulations' raising compliance costs.
SWOT threat -- increasing competition across domestic and international markets may affect the Company's ability to sustain market share and profitability.

risks.risk: Supply chain disruption, logistics cost inflation and market volatility
risks.note: Rising logistics costs and geopolitical uncertainties may impact profitability; fluctuations in global economic activity, geopolitical events and international trade dynamics may influence demand, input costs and export performance.

risks.risk: Enterprise risk categories flagged by the Board (competition, credit, ESG, raw material, concentration, cyber security)
risks.note: The Board's Report Risk Management section names competition risk, credit risk, ESG risk, raw material risk, concentration risk and cyber security risk as exposures the Company manages under its Risk Management Policy, overseen by the Risk Management Committee.

one-line thesis: Indo Count is transitioning from a pure-play exporter to a diversified global home textiles player, with utility bedding and branded segments scaling rapidly despite US tariff headwinds; the near-term margin pressure is strategic to secure long-term market share and brand equity, with a clear path to margin recovery post-tariff stabilization and full capacity ramp-up.
financial scorecard: Revenue: +12% QoQ to ₹1,082cr (driven by new business); EBITDA: +3% QoQ to ₹123cr, margin down 90bps to 11.4% (tariff sharing + brand ramp-up costs); PAT: ₹39cr (flat QoQ); Order Book: Rolling 50-day visibility, Q3 volumes similar to Q2; Net Debt: Reduced ₹175cr in H1 FY26, Net Debt/Equity at 0.34x (no one-offs, but margin compression due to strategic tariff support)
guidance: Revenue growth: USD 275M by FY28 (USD 175M utility bedding + USD 100M brands); Margin: Core business to return to 15-16% EBITDA margin in 6-9 months; Order inflow: Steady, no cancellations; Capex/Commissioning: USD 15M NC facility to ramp by Dec 2025/Jan 2026; FY26 CAPEX ~₹215cr (mostly US facilities), FY27 only maintenance CAPEX planned
order book & pipeline: Rolling 50-day visibility; Q3 volumes expected to match Q2 levels; no major cancellations despite tariff pressure
segment / subsidiary detail: Core Business: 25.2M meters sold in Q2 (+7% QoQ); 700 new retail counters added in India; Utility Bedding: 2/3 of new business run-rate ($85M pa); 31M pillow capacity across 3 US plants; Brand Business: 1/3 of new business run-rate ($85M pa); 4 brands (Wamsutta, Fieldcrest, Waverly, Gaiam); Tommy Hilfiger & Beautyrest under utility bedding segment only
growth verticals / optionality: Expansion into UK, Australia, Japan, Middle East via new FTAs; domestic retail footprint growth (Boutique Living, Layers); potential licensing of additional premium brands; utility bedding capacity utilization to drive higher margins post-ramp-up
margins & cost dynamics: Core EBITDA margin compressed by 84bps QoQ due to tariff-sharing (Russian oil penalty + 50% US tariff); brand/utility ramp-up adding 150-200bps EBITDA drag; target margins: utility bedding 15-16%, branded 17-18%; cost savings via supply chain optimization underway
capex / expansion: FY26 CAPEX: ₹215cr (₹99cr for NC Greenfield; ₹49cr spent so far; ₹31cr spent in FY25); NC facility: $15M investment; ZLD project at Billard to spill into FY27; no major CAPEX planned for FY27 beyond maintenance
capital allocation: Debt reduction of ₹175cr in H1 FY26; focus on deleveraging while funding US expansion; no dividend or buyback mentioned; future allocation to sustain brand marketing and capacity utilization, not equity dilution
risks & watch-items: Prolonged 50% US tariff; consumer demand slowdown in US post-price pass-through; delayed NC facility ramp-up; failure to achieve brand margin targets; currency volatility; FTA ratification delays (UK, EU)
management quality / tone: Confident and strategic; acknowledges short-term margin pressure as intentional to protect market share; emphasizes long-term brand equity and diversification; optimistic on tariff resolution and domestic growth; transparent on challenges but avoids disclosing sensitive customer discount details
non-obvious takeaways: Wamsutta’s 50-state sales in 45 days indicates exceptional brand recall and DTC execution capability — a rare success in home textiles; utility bedding’s US manufacturing is not just tariff-proof but also enables faster inventory turnover and higher ASPs than export-bound core business

| Challenge | Beneficiary/Loser | Dir | Conviction | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| US 50% tariff on Indian home textiles | Indo Count Industries Limited | beneficiary | High | Tariff pressure is accelerating shift to US-based manufacturing and branded business, which are higher-margin and tariff-immune — turning a threat into strategic advantage |
| Declining ASP in core exports due to down-trading | Indo Count Industries Limited | beneficiary | High | Company is proactively pivoting to premiumization via Wamsutta and Tommy Hilfiger, reducing reliance on commoditized exports |

themes.title: Textiles - apparel/home-textile exports + synthetics
themes.need: India textiles ride three tailwinds at once: China+1 sourcing shifts, the India-UK FTA (signed) + India-EU FTA (advancing), and US tariff normalization - favouring apparel exporters (GOKEX/PGIL/PDSL) and US-heavy home-textile names (WELSPUNLIV/HIMATSEIDE). A second leg = value-added synthetics/recycling (FILATEX, SANATHAN, CENTENKA, GANECOS) and cotton-yarn spread recovery (VTL/NITINSPIN/SPORTKING) plus branded apparel (PAGEIND, ARVIND, RAYMONDLSL).
themes.driver: FTA implementation + US-India trade-deal clarity; festive/wedding demand; cotton-yarn spread; anti-dumping rulings.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- India-EU Free Trade Agreement, concluded January 2026, grants zero-duty access to the EU market for Indian textiles, apparel and made-ups, eliminating prior duties of 8-12% and restoring tariff parity with Bangladesh and Vietnam; expected to strengthen trade flows and improve long-term visibility for Indian home textile exporters.
- Within U.S. cotton textiles, the home textiles segment (cotton bed linen, towels, made-ups) is projected to grow at an 8.9% CAGR, presenting a constructive medium-term demand backdrop for established Indian manufacturers serving the U.S. retail channel.
- Bed linen remains Indo Count's dominant product category in the global home textiles market, with bathroom linen emerging as a faster-growing adjacency.
- U.S. home textiles retail continues shifting toward omnichannel models, with rapid e-commerce and direct-to-consumer expansion enabling deeper customer reach and engagement.
- India's structural advantages -- world's largest cotton producer, second-largest employer after agriculture, and an integrated cotton-to-finished-product value chain -- support established manufacturers amid the 'China-plus-one' sourcing realignment.
- Government of India's Ministry of Textiles has outlined a roadmap to triple textile exports from ₹3 lakh crore today to ₹9 lakh crore by 2030, supported by stronger domestic manufacturing and broader global market outreach.
- Growing global-buyer emphasis on eco-friendly and traceable cotton sourcing is emerging as a defining lever, presenting a premium opportunity for manufacturers with integrated procurement and certified traceability frameworks.
- New businesses (utility bedding and the U.S. brand business) scaled from 2% of revenue in FY23 to 19% in FY26, reaching an annualised run rate above USD 100 million -- management frames this as a new revenue vertical approaching a fifth of total income built within three years.

margins.title: Margins & cost dynamics
margins.body: Core EBITDA margin compressed by 84bps QoQ due to tariff-sharing (Russian oil penalty + 50% US tariff); brand/utility ramp-up adding 150-200bps EBITDA drag; target margins: utility bedding 15-16%, branded 17-18%; cost savings via supply chain optimization underway

capital_allocation.title: Capital allocation
capital_allocation.body: Debt reduction of ₹175cr in H1 FY26; focus on deleveraging while funding US expansion; no dividend or buyback mentioned; future allocation to sustain brand marketing and capacity utilization, not equity dilution

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: The largest capacity addition in FY26 was Indo Count's first and largest overseas greenfield manufacturing facility, at Kernersville, North Carolina, for utility bedding; it commenced commercial production in January 2026, adding 18 million pillows/year and taking combined U.S. pillow capacity to 31 million units alongside 1.5 million quilts, with the three U.S. facilities (Columbus OH, Phoenix AZ, Kernersville NC) together providing East Coast, Midwest and West Coast coverage. On the brand side, Wamsutta (the Company's fully owned legacy U.S. brand) was relaunched in July 2025 on a Direct-to-Consumer platform and reached all 50 U.S. states within 45 days; a new licensing agreement with Tommy Hilfiger for utility bedding was signed during the year, taking the licensed-brand count to six (Fieldcrest, Waverly, GAIAM, Jasper Conran, Beautyrest, Tommy Hilfiger). Domestically, the Boutique Living and Layers brands added 700 new counters in a single quarter, entered the bath and gifting segments, and now reach about 2,000 touchpoints, though the domestic business remains young at 2.25% of revenue with management expecting it to become a meaningful contributor over three to five years. Core business capacity utilisation stood at 60-65%, and the two existing U.S. utility bedding facilities were also running at 60-65% utilisation. Total capital expenditure during FY26 was ₹202 crore. Looking ahead, the Company has planned ₹250 crore of capital expenditure over the next 12-18 months, three-quarters funded by internal accruals, comprising ₹95 crore for a Zero Liquid Discharge facility at the Bhilad unit, ₹85 crore for a spinning brownfield expansion and modernisation, and ₹70 crore of maintenance capex, framed as support for the goal of doubling revenues by 2028.

management_tone.title: Management quality / tone
management_tone.body: Confident and strategic; acknowledges short-term margin pressure as intentional to protect market share; emphasizes long-term brand equity and diversification; optimistic on tariff resolution and domestic growth; transparent on challenges but avoids disclosing sensitive customer discount details

litigation.title: Litigation & compliance (profile)
litigation.body: {"material": "false", "note": "Board's Report states that during the year under review no significant or material orders were passed by the Regulators, Courts or Tribunals which impact the going concern status and the Company's future operations.", "as_of": "2026-08-03"}

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Vertically integrated manufacturing from spinning to finished bed linen across four Indian facilities (Alte, Gokul Shirgaon, Bhilad, Kagal), enabling efficient capacity utilisation and operational synergies.
- Diversified owned and licensed brand portfolio (Boutique Living, Layers, and the revived heritage brand Wamsutta, alongside licensed brands Fieldcrest, Waverly, Beautyrest and Tommy Hilfiger) supporting premiumisation and B2C/D2C channel diversification beyond traditional B2B.
- Demonstrated customer-relationship durability: through the peak-tariff disruption of FY26 the Company retained every customer and fulfilled every order without cancellation, strengthening its standing from supplier to indispensable partner.
- Local U.S. manufacturing footprint (Phoenix AZ, Kernersville NC, Columbus OH) brings production closer to its largest market (~70% of market exposure), improving fulfilment speed and supply-chain responsiveness, while U.S.-cotton content above 20% qualifies for proportionate tariff relief in the premium segment.
- Broad sustainability/quality certification base (OEKO-TEX STeP, ISO 9001/14001/45001, LEED Green Building, NABL/ISO 17025) plus a leading ESG profile (S&P Global ESG score of 78, top 3 percentile globally in the sector) that supports trust with global retail customers.
- Recognised export leadership — six consecutive TEXPROCIL Gold Trophies for the highest exports of bed sheets/bed linen in the cotton made-ups category.

risks.title: Risks & watch-items
risks.body: Prolonged 50% US tariff; consumer demand slowdown in US post-price pass-through; delayed NC facility ramp-up; failure to achieve brand margin targets; currency volatility; FTA ratification delays (UK, EU)

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious takeaways
non_obvious.body: Wamsutta’s 50-state sales in 45 days indicates exceptional brand recall and DTC execution capability — a rare success in home textiles; utility bedding’s US manufacturing is not just tariff-proof but also enables faster inventory turnover and higher ASPs than export-bound core business

challenges.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers
challenges.body:
| Challenge | Beneficiary/Loser | Dir | Conviction | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| US 50% tariff on Indian home textiles | Indo Count Industries Limited | beneficiary | High | Tariff pressure is accelerating shift to US-based manufacturing and branded business, which are higher-margin and tariff-immune — turning a threat into strategic advantage |
| Declining ASP in core exports due to down-trading | Indo Count Industries Limited | beneficiary | High | Company is proactively pivoting to premiumization via Wamsutta and Tommy Hilfiger, reducing reliance on commoditized exports |

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [Acquisition] Entered pillow and quilt manufacturing in the USA "via acquisition & greenfield"; the investment chart footnote names a Fluvitex acquisition, with payment stated on a 100% basis.
- [Trade policy] Chairman cites the implementation of the India-UK Free Trade Agreement and progress on US and EU trade negotiations, and attributes the Q1FY27 start to "the normalization of the US tariff scenario"; easing of U.S. tariff uncertainty is credited with supporting recovery in demand and order flow.
- [Industry share data] Otexa (June 2026) data on USA import share is presented for cotton sheets, cotton pillowcases and cotton bedspreads & quilts across CY21-Jan-Jun 26 for India, Pakistan, China and ROW; the extraction does not reliably bind each percentage series to its country label, so no share figures are asserted here.
- [Awards] Won the TEXPROCIL Gold Trophy (25th May 2026) for the highest exports of bed sheets/bed linen in the Cotton Made-ups category for 2023-2024, the 6th consecutive year of the award.
- [Channel context] US e-commerce cited at 23.8% of total retail sales in Q1 2026 with unadjusted US e-commerce sales of $302.3 billion in Q1 2026 (Source: Digital Commerce 360).
